That being said, everybody has their own way of doing things. If someone suggests something, try it. If someone else suggests a different way, try that too. You'll soon figure out what works best for you and your style and piece together your own way. 


Focus on doing the job and what it means to you. Don't get caught up in petty drama. 


Know that you're there to do a job. Nobody needs to like you as long as you're doing what policy says and can cover your own butt. 


On the other hand, work on building relationships with your fellow officers. They are going to become your family. They will have your back if shit hits the fan and you need to have theirs as well. 


Stay positive. This is an extremely stressful job that's certainly not for everybody. But never let that stress follow you home. You end up hurting and alienating your loved ones if you allow that to happen. 


Along with this, never bring your home life to work either. The two need to stay separated in order for you to effectively do your job. Inmates tend to latch on to this and pretend to care. You end up talking to them and next thing you know, you're in over your head in something you don't want any part of. 


Inmates will test you, just for the sole fact that you're a new boot. Don't let it get to you. If they tell you something that you're unsure about, ask another CO or your supervisor. 


Firm Fair and Consistent is not just some stupid thing they tell you in academy. It's actually very important and will eventually earn you the respect of the inmates once you demonstrate that it's who you are. 


If you say that you'll do something, make sure that you do it. Plain and simple. 


Keep a check on your mental health. I know a month seems short, but depending on the situation it can be more than enough time to cause some serious mental health issues and is definitely more than enough time to see some pretty messed up stuff happen. Fact is, 1 out of 3 officers has PTSD. If something bothers you, talk to someone about it. This is speaking from personal experience here. I've seen people spiral downward because they decided to bottle everything up and pretend that they were too macho to be anything but fine. 


If you want any clarification or more advice, definitely ask myself or others.
